1.why: Two complete sign pairs (±6, ±1) with no asymmetry, so nothing distinguishes the four; picked the larger positive.

2.why: 400 is the derivational hub: 1200 = 3x400, 120 = 400x0.3, 403 = 400+3, so the other three are all slips off it.

3.why: Exact 2x2 cross product of x in {5,-1} and y in {-9,-1}; every coordinate appears twice, so the set alone narrows nothing.

4.why: -0.5 is the only non-integer and the only negative, and 2 is its negative reciprocal (the un-negated/un-inverted slip).

5.why: Full 2x2 cross of the two sign choices in numerator and denominator; each factor appears exactly twice, so shape alone is balanced.

6.why: One sign pair (±32) against two unpaired small values; betting the positive member of the pair, its negative being the sign-error distractor.

7.why: One sign pair (±7) with 10 and 25 unpaired; positive member of the pair.

8.why: Two complete sign pairs (±3, ±4), perfectly symmetric; no structural discriminator.

9.why: Splits two-and-two (odd squares 9 and 25 against small negatives -1, -2) with no lone outlier; picked a square.

10.why: Non-numeric set that does narrow by shape: A is the malformed rate-divided-by-period form and D is the only canonical 1 + r/n compounding form.

11.why: 18 is the hub and the positive member of the ±18 pair: 324 = 18^2 and 81 = (18/2)^2 both derive from it.

12.why: Sign pair (±10) and hub agree: 5 = 10/2 and -2 = -10/5 are both derived from 10.

13.why: Non-numeric: exact 2x2 cross of endpoint pair {-2,8} vs {-8,2} and interior-vs-exterior; balanced by shape, no leak.

14.why: No lone form - 20 and 120 are round, 44 and 72 are not - so no outlier to bet on.

15.why: Sign pair (±27) and hub agree: 27 = 3^3 with 9 = 3^2 derived from it, so the positive 27.

16.why: -1/3 is simultaneously the only fraction, the only negative and the only non-integer - the lone odd-formatted value.

17.why: 8 is the hub reaching all three others: 8^2 = 64, 8/2 = 4, and 49 = 7^2 is the off-by-one-base square.

18.why: 9 is the hub: 81 = 9^2, 3 = sqrt(9), 36 = 9x4, so the other three are operations applied to it.

19.why: 1/3 is the only fraction in an otherwise integer set, with 3 its reciprocal partner (the un-inverted slip).

20.why: Non-numeric: exact 2x2 cross product of x in {12,3} and y in {5,10}; the set alone narrows nothing.

21.why: 2.5 is the only non-integer against three integers - lone odd-formatted value.

22.why: 79 is a magnitude outlier but not a form outlier, and no two values are related arithmetically; picked among the small integers.

23.why: 48.8 + 51.2 = 100, a complementary percentage pair that narrows the set to two; 51.2 = 0.8x64 ties cleanly to another option.

24.why: 0 is the only non-positive value but differs in kind rather than form, and 5, 6, 9 are unrelated; low-confidence outlier bet.
